messages:
chao: Nightly microbench sweep finished. A few candidate kernels regressed badly at seqlen=2048 on A100s — end-to-end throughput down ~2x vs baseline for model_xxl. Uploaded logs to GCS.
perf-bot: CI summary: nightly-seq-sweep/2026-03-16 — 3 candidates failed threshold at seqlen=2048, 0 failures at <=1024. Link: https://gcs.redwood-internal/nightly/seq-sweep/1830001234/report.html :rotating_light:
chao: Quick paste of the odd output from microprobe run:```bash
# run on a single A100
./kernel_probe --kernel candidate_7 --model model_xxl --seqlen 2048 --steps 200
Throughput: 18.7 samples/s (baseline: 38.9 samples/s)
GPU mem util: 63%  KV cache misses: +large spikes around step 42-48
```
maria_g: Hmm KV cache spikes. Is this the same candidate that switches to the 'wide-matmul' path for long seqlen? I saw a codepath that toggles block-size at 1536.
alex: yeah candidate_7 uses tiled-wmma for seqlen >= 1536 on Ampere. It gives good perf on 4096 in synthetic single-op bench, but combined with our KV cache streaming it seems to thrash. Might be working set alignment issues.
sara: @chao can you share a minimal reproducer that includes the KV cache warmup pattern? we need to triage whether it's a kernel memory access pattern or our cache manager.
chao: repro attached inline:```py
# minimal repro: simulate KV warmup + streaming decode
from runtime import InferenceHarness
h = InferenceHarness(model='model_xxl', device='a100')
# warmup prefixes cause interleaved cache allocations
for i in range(64):
    h.decode(prefix_length=1024 if i%2==0 else 512, seq=256)
# heavy long-seq run
r = h.decode(prefix_length=2048, seq=512, kernel='candidate_7', steps=200)
print(r.throughput)
```
perf-bot: Attached perf counters (pinned): L2_hit_ratio drop ~12% when switching to tiled-wmma path, DRAM bandwidth oscillation coincides with KV flush events.
maria_g: That points to working set + kernel tile size mismatch. Two follow-ups: 1) autotuner should evaluate candidates per seqlen bucket (e.g., <=512, 513-1536, 1537-3072) not just average latency; 2) harness should simulate realistic KV warmups so we don't select winners that only work in sterile microbench.
eng-ci: Agreed. Proposing CI changes: - add seqlen buckets into nightly sweep matrix - run candidate kernels with KV-warmup fixture - mark flaky candidates with warning instead of auto-promote. Example YAML:```yaml
nightly_seq_sweep:
  matrix:
    seqlen: [256, 1024, 2048]
    kv_warmup: [true, false]
  thresholds:
    pass_pct: 95
    warn_on_flaky: true
```
alex: Also, small runtime mitigation: if KV cache miss rate > 8% during first 100 steps, fall back to baseline kernel (less tiling) for next 500 steps and signal autotuner to re-evaluate with warmup policy. I can sketch the check.
sara: +1 on both CI and runtime mitigation. That fallback buys us safety while we refine the autotuner. Can we add a lightweight regression test to perf CI that runs the failing candidate in a controlled way?
chao: I'll own the harness changes. Plan: 1) add seqlen buckets and kv_warmup fixture to nightly (eng-ci ok?), 2) add a synthetic regression test that runs candidate_7 on A100 with kv_warmup and asserts throughput >= 0.8 * baseline, 3) add a runtime guard with metrics threshold. Target PR by tomorrow EOD.
eng-ci: Sounds good. Please include the exact GCS path for failing artifacts in the PR template so SRE can triage hardware noise: gs://nightly-artifacts/seq-sweep/1830001234/*.
maria_g: One more ask: can the autotuner store per-arch, per-seqlen best-candidate rather than a single best-candidate across all seqlens? That removes brittle global winners.
alex: yes it's a straightforward keying change, but we need to bound storage. Suggest sharded policy: keep top-2 per (arch,seqlen_bucket).
chao: noted. I'll include metadata changes in the PR. Quick WIP snippet for the autotuner update:```py
def key_for_tuner(arch, seqlen):
    if seqlen <= 512: b='s'
    elif seqlen <= 1536: b='m'
    else: b='l'
    return f"{arch}:{b}"
```
sara: Great. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup: chao please drop the PR link here when ready and mark it with "perf-regress" label.
chao: Will do — pushing local tests now, will open PR when green.
